Almond is the founder of Almond Athletics.[http://almondathletics.com/about About Us | Almond Athletics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160327004431/http://almondathletics.com/about/ |date=2016-03-27 }}. Retrieved on March 4, 2024. His last professional appearance would be for the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League). ==High school== {{Expand section|date=June 2025}} Almond was born in [[Dalton, Georgia]] and attended [[McEachern High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]], where he was a teammate of fellow professional basketball player [[Josh Smith]]. Almond was the first basketball player in McEachern school history to have his #22 jersey retired.{{cn|date=June 2025}} ==College career== Almond played college basketball at [[Rice University]], where he was a member of [[Residential Colleges of Rice University|Martel residential college]].{{cite web|title=Smooth Shooter|url=http://news.rice.edu/2006/11/16/smooth-shooter/|work=Rice News|publisher=Rice University News & Media|access-date=21 February 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714151001/http://news.rice.edu/2006/11/16/smooth-shooter/|url-status=dead}} During his junior season, Almond's scoring average jumped to 21.9 points per game (up from 7.2 points per game as a sophomore). His scoring average led all players in [[Conference USA]]. During his senior year, Almond's scoring average increased to 26.4 points per game, ranking third in the nation. He was named Conference USA Player of the Year and was named AP All-America Honorable Mention. Almond finished his career at Rice with 121 games played and a scoring average of 15.1 points per game. He was also the first Rice basketball player to appear on the cover of a national publication.{{cite web|title=Smooth Shooter|url=http://news.rice.edu/2006/11/16/smooth-shooter/|work=Rice News|publisher=Rice University News & Media|access-date=21 February 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714151001/http://news.rice.edu/2006/11/16/smooth-shooter/|url-status=dead}} After graduation, he was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the first round (25th pick) in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== Almond played in 9 games during his rookie season with the Jazz, averaging 4.3 minutes. His NBA career high is currently 12 points, at [[Sacramento Kings|Sacramento]] on December 2, 2008. He scored his first NBA points on January 8, 2008, against the [[Indiana Pacers]], with 2 points on 1-of-5 shooting. However, he spent most of the season with the team's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate, the [[Utah Flash]], to whom he was assigned.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/utah/almond_071206.html |title=Jazz Assigns Morris Almond and Kyrylo Fesenko To Utah Flash |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100524115728/http://www.nba.com/dleague/utah/almond_071206.html |archive-date=2010-05-24 |url-status=dead }} He led the D-League in scoring during the season, averaging 25.6 points per game.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/statistics/player/Scoring.jsp?league=20&season=22007&conf=OVERALL&position=0&splitType=9&splitScope=GAME&qualified=Y&yearsExp=-1&splitDD=All%20Teams |title=NBA D-League – 2007–08 scoring average |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-04-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106133938/http://www.nba.com/dleague/statistics/player/Scoring.jsp?league=20&season=22007&conf=OVERALL&position=0&splitType=9&splitScope=GAME&qualified=Y&yearsExp=-1&splitDD=All%20Teams |archive-date=2012-11-06 |url-status=dead }} In just his fifth game with the team on December 21, 2007, he tied a league record with 51 points in a 118–116 victory over the [[Austin Toros]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20071221/AUSUTA/recap.html Almond Ties D-League Record, Flash Outlast Toros] Later in the season, he broke the record with a 53-point performance against the [[Bakersfield Jam]] in a 102–87 win.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/Almond_Leads_Flash_to_10287_W-255515-1172.html Almond Leads Flash to 102–87 Win Over Jam] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106134113/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/Almond_Leads_Flash_to_10287_W-255515-1172.html |date=2012-11-06 }}. The record was tied by [[Will Conroy]] in 2009 and surpassed by [[Pierre Jackson]] in 2014 (58).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10406002/idaho-star-pierre-jackson-scores-d-league-record-58-points|title=Pierre Jackson's 58 D-League best|access-date=2014-02-05|date=2014-02-04|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On September 18, 2009, Morris Almond signed with the [[Orlando Magic]]. [http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic_sign_almond_johnson_prepare_camp_091809.html Magic Sign Almond, Johnson; Prepare for Camp] He was waived on October 21, 2009.[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62267/20091021/orlando_waives_morris_almond/ Orlando Waives Morris Almond] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091023133054/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62267/20091021/orlando_waives_morris_almond/ |date=2009-10-23 }}. Retrieved on October 21, 2009. Almond later played for the [[Maine Red Claws]] and [[Springfield Armor]] of the NBA Development League.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=morris_almond Morris Almond playerfile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091230050910/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=morris_almond |date=2009-12-30 }}. NBA Development League. He then signed with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] of the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]]. In July 2010 he left Real Madrid and joined the Italian club [[Scavolini Pesaro]].[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/07/scavolini-pesaro-signs-morris-almond.html Scavolini Pesaro signs Morris Almond ] In January 2012, Almond returned to the United States and signed with the Maine Red Claws for the second time.{{cite news|url=http://www.masslive.com/sports/index.ssf/2012/01/new-look_armor_red_claws_meet.html|title=New-look Armor, Red Claws meet for third straight time Thursday night |work=[[The Republican (Springfield)|The Republican]]|access-date=19 January 2012}} On the 16th of April 2012, the Washington Wizards announced they would be signing Almond to contract for the rest of the 2011–12 season.[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards_sign_morris_almond_2012_04_16.html WIZARDS SIGN GUARD MORRIS ALMOND] At the end of the 2011–2012 season he was selected to the All NBA D-League Third Team after averaging 23.4 points and 6.0 rebounds per game for the Red Claws. Almond briefly played for [[KK Crvena Zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] during the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/rastanak-sa-almondom |title=RASTANAK SA ALMONDOM |access-date=2012-10-21 |archive-date=2012-10-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023212905/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/rastanak-sa-almondom |url-status=dead }} He then returned to the Maine Red Claws, who traded him to the [[Iowa Energy]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |title=2012–13 Transactions |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101144313/http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |archive-date=2011-11-01 |url-status=dead }} On January 30, 2013, he and [[Mike Taylor (basketball player)|Mike Taylor]] were traded to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] in exchange for Jarrid Famous.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130216122811/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130130_almond_taylor.html|title=D-Fenders Acquire Morris Almond and Mike Taylor}} ==Post-professional career== Almond has since retired from professional basketball. He formed Almond Athletics, a non-profit organization, in 2013.[http://almondathletics.com/about About Us | Almond Athletics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160327004431/http://almondathletics.com/about/|date=2016-03-27}}.
